# The quotient generated by short ordinary mutation returns

**PROVED IN NOTE, conditional only on the explicitly inherited short-return
classification. FINITE-EXACT controls below.** This classifies connectivity
generated by ordinary tournament returns of length at most four. It does not
classify unrestricted quiver mutation classes, and it gives no new H values.

## Inheritance and operation

The source is a finite tournament T with skew matrix B, where b_ij=1 for
i->j, b_ji=-b_ij and b_ii=0. Ordinary Fomin--Zelevinsky mutation at k is

    b'_ij=-b_ij                              if i=k or j=k,
    b'_ij=b_ij+(|b_ik|b_kj+b_ik|b_kj|)/2     otherwise.

Intermediate entries remain arbitrary integers. No sign projection, filling
of holes, or deletion of multiplicities is permitted. A short return has
tournament endpoints and at most four such steps.

Closest proved mechanism: [FOUR_RETURNS](../../triples_ports_sieve_20261112/ports/FOUR_RETURNS.md)
and its [independent audit](../../triples_ports_sieve_20261112/ports/AUDIT_FOUR.md).
The native SCC hull and shorter return classifications are in
[ports PROOF](../../triples_ports_sieve_20261112/ports/PROOF.md), sections1--2;
the named pentagon is in [Session291 cluster theorem3](../../session291_cluster_ports_20261113/cluster/PROOF.md).
The hostile is a strong four-vertex tournament: it has H=5 but no source,
sink or extreme triangle factor. The useful sidecar is the ordered SCC word,
not merely its product H. Our board is short word / SCC factor / rigid hull /
cyclic exterior word / named transport / scalar count.

The inherited four-step proof is genuinely all-order. It restricts entry
conditions to the mutated vertices and two entry endpoints, then derives
the global ordinal operations; it does not infer H-invariance from local H.
Its five reduced four-letter shapes are0101,0102,0120,0121,0123. The
three-letter genuine excursion is010; the nonnative new four-letter family
0120 transports an extreme C3 factor and reverses that factor. Every short
return preserves H. These are inherited statements, not new proofs here.

## M1. Short-return reachability has a complete SCC description

Pass to ordinary unlabelled tournament classes. Write the unique ordered
SCC word of T. Its possible small letters are C1 (a singleton) and C3 (the
unique directed triangle). Call an SCC **large here** if it has at least four
vertices; this word is only a size convention, not modular indecomposability.

**Theorem.** The equivalence relation generated by all short returns is
exactly the relation generated by moving an extreme C1 or C3 SCC to the
opposite end of the SCC word. Every large SCC keeps its isomorphism type,
and the linear interval from the first through last large SCC is unchanged.

Proof of necessity. A native source/sink step moves one extreme C1. The
010 transitive-pair transfer moves two consecutive extreme C1 factors;
its reversal of their labels changes no unlabelled SCC type. Shape0101 is
a native move followed by relabelling. Shapes0102 and0121 split into a
native step and a shorter return. Shape0123 moves four successive extreme
C1 factors. Shape0120 moves one extreme C3, whose converse is isomorphic
to C3, while leaving the exterior unchanged. Consecutive equal mutations
cancel. The separately inherited orders1--3 exceptions introduce no other
unlabelled SCC word. Every short return is therefore generated by the
stated end moves. Conversely C1 transport is one ordinary mutation and
C3 transport is the literal four-letter word0120. QED.

This theorem concerns the generated relation, not a claim that its graph
is a simple path: a short return may jump across several consecutive C1
letters. Named relabellings in0101 are also deliberately quotiented here.

### With a large SCC

Let K be the fixed SCC interval from the first through last large SCC,
including every internal singleton and triangle. Write T=A -> K -> D,
where A,D are words over C1,C3. Its complete component invariant is

    (K, F=D A).

For F=f_1...f_m the component consists of precisely the m+1 classes

    f_(j+1)...f_m -> K -> f_1...f_j,       0<=j<=m.

Every displayed cut is reached by moving one end factor at a time. They
are distinct because the number and ordered types of SCCs before the first
large component differ. No exterior factor can pass through K one at a
time; it passes around the whole tournament. Thus internal C1/C3 factors
cannot become exterior through this operation language.

### With no large SCC

The component consists exactly of the distinct cyclic rotations of the word
over C1,C3. Its invariant is therefore a binary necklace with letter weights
1 and3. Periodic words have fewer distinct rotations. The empty tournament
is treated as one isolated class when counting order0.

## M2. A complete ordinary-class quotient formula

Let A(x)=sum_(n>=0) a_n x^n be the ordinary tournament class series
(A000568), a_0=1, and put P(x)=1/(1-x-x^3). The series of possible rigid
intervals K in M1 is

    K(x)=(1-x-x^3)^2 A(x)-(1-x-x^3).

Indeed every tournament either is a word entirely over C1,C3, or has the
unique decomposition A -> K -> D. Thus A=P+P^2 K.

Let N(x) count nonempty weighted binary necklaces:

    N(x)=sum_(d>=1) phi(d)/d * log(1/(1-x^d-x^(3d))).

This formal series has integer coefficients. Burnside's cyclic rotation
lemma gives the formula: a rotation of a length-l word with cycles of length
d fixes repetitions of a word whose letter weights are multiplied by d;
summing phi(d) such rotations and dividing by l yields the logarithm.

**Corollary.** If c_n counts components generated by all short returns on
ordinary n-vertex tournament classes, then

    C(x)=sum c_n x^n=(1-x-x^3) A(x)+N(x).               (1)

The rigid-hull part is K P, and the no-large part is1+N; substitution yields
(1). This is a quotient of known a_n, not an algorithm extending unknown
A000568 values. The directly checked n=0,...,5 counts are

    a_n=1,1,1,2,4,12;     c_n=1,1,1,2,3,9.

The new triangle transport starts merging previously separate native
components at order7: C4 -> C3 and C3 -> C4 are connected by0120 although
neither graph has a global source/sink. Their common count is15. C4 denotes
the unique strong four-vertex tournament, not a directed four-cycle digraph.

## M3. The prime and7p lanes keep their actual strong core

**Corollary.** A strong tournament of order at least four is pointwise fixed
by every short return on its named matrix.

There is no native first/last step, no extreme TT2 or TT4, and no extreme
proper C3. Every reduced word shape in the inherited classification is
therefore impossible. Only cancellations remain, and these give the exact
original labelled matrix. This is stronger than scalar H-preservation but
is restricted to short returns.

If a tournament has prime H=p>=5, it has exactly one nontrivial SCC, of
count p and order at least4. If H=7p, p prime, with7 and21 excluded, the
same holds: more than one nontrivial SCC would force an SCC of count7,
which is impossible by **THM-1370**,
[h-spectrum-omits-7-21-all-n](../../../../01-canon/theorems/THM-1370-h-spectrum-omits-7-21-all-n.md).
Every nontrivial SCC has H>=3, and an H=1 tournament is transitive.

Consequently these source classes are TT_a -> K -> TT_b with K large and
strong. Under any number of short returns their unlabelled component is
exactly the inherited native component: only singleton padding moves, and
K remains the same actual isomorphism type. The triangle family cannot
improve the unlabelled source menu in these lanes. This does not freeze
fixed physical port names: a relabelling changes which old root response
sits at that name. Only covariantly transported marks preserve rooted
isomorphism type. The next construction makes that distinction executable.

Longer ordinary excursions are not excluded. Any H-changing tournament
path must contain a consecutive tournament-to-tournament segment of length
at least5 with no intervening tournament. This lower bound does not assert
the existence of such a segment or bound the length required.

## M4. A singleton buffer permits actual fixed-name root switching

Suppose v is a global source or sink and u is any other vertex. Write

    Q(u,v)=u v u v.

The inherited0101 identity says Q(u,v)B=tau_(u,v) mu_v(B), which is a
tournament because v was extreme. Its extreme buffer label becomes u
and its source/sink side reverses.

If u,w are two distinct non-buffer names, perform

    Q(u,v), Q(w,u), Q(v,w), v.                          (2)

After the three Q words the extreme buffer label is respectively u,w,v,
so each hypothesis holds; the final mutation at v is native. Equivariance
shows that two Q words act as tau_(w,u) tau_(u,v): their two native
mutations cancel. Three act as tau_(u,w) mu_v, and the last mutation at v
cancels that remaining mu_v. Thus the final matrix is exactly tau_(u,w)B.
This is an actual13-mutation program with tournament checkpoints
after4,8,12,13. No minimum-length claim is made. Every name persists.
Iterating such swaps
implements any desired permutation of the non-buffer names while returning
the buffer to the same extreme position.

For example use C1 -> C4, with buffer0 and C4 adjacency rows(2,4,9,3)
on names1,2,3,4. Swapping names1 and3 by(2) leaves H=5 but changes the
deletion count at fixed name1 from3 to1. This is a literal marked-response
change. It selects a response already present among the old vertices;
it does not create a new intrinsic rooted isomorphism type or a previously
absent ready root. Joint ports transform by the same known permutation,
so the full joint data can be transported without confusing the fixed-name
and covariant conventions.

This route is available to padded prime/7p sources even though the bare
strong core is pointwise frozen under a single short return. A universal
induction still needs a source having the required response somewhere;
the transport theorem supplies a legal named selector when it exists.

## Connection contract and validation

Source: an actual integer quiver word with tournament endpoints. Target:
the SCC necklace/rigid-hull invariant. The map preserves unlabelled
short-return reachability and H, but forgets intermediate weighted quivers,
vertex names and port attachments. A literal word and marked input graph
restore those data. Prime arithmetic alone does not restore them.

The accompanying checker constructs ordinary representatives through order5,
tests every reduced word shape of lengths1--4 under every injective naming,
and compares resulting components with the independently computed SCC
invariant. It additionally replays the literal C4/C3 transfer at order7
and the marked singleton-buffer program at order5.
Its finite tests corroborate M1; the inherited all-order word classification
and the proof above supply its quantifiers.
